page.running_head: SECT. I. PART. I. CAP. X.

main_text.p: ctio & maturatio, fusio & liquefactio, aper-tio & dilatatio; Exiccatio, humectatio, e-mollitio, condensatio & terminatio, debili-tatio, ustio, consumtio.
main_text.head: Ἔκθεσις[?]
main_text.p: I. Actionum harum varietas & contrarietas quo-que è variâ materiæ dispositione oritur, ut è sequen-tibus patebit. Attenuat calor partes crassiores re-solvendo & incidendo: coquit & maturat attenuan-do, cruditates absumendo, & dissipando, homoge-nea magis magisque congregando; fundit & liquefacit ea, quæ à frigore sunt concreta, & humore abun-dant, frigus tanquam vinculum Concretorum frangendo, expellendo, & partes humidas resol-vendo: aperit & dilatat partes in poris contentas re-solvendo, attenuando,&evocando. Undè vulgò po-ri à calore dicuntur aperiri, extracto & consumto humore crassiori, quo erant oeclusi & repleti: exsic-cat partes humidiores resolvendo & evocando, re-lictis terrestribus: Humectat humorem frigore con-cretum resolvendo, attenuando,& fluidum redden-do: Emollit humectando: Condensat duobus potissimum modis: (1) humidum evocando: dum enim corpora incalescunt, tenuiores humidi partes evaporant, terrestres relinquuntur, sic lutum à calore indura-tur & condensatur. (2) Humidum cum sicco terre-stri commiscendo; dum enim corpora rarefacit, hu-midum per omnes sicci partes promtè diffunditur, & sicco terrestri exactè permiscetur, unde humidi con-defatio & terminatio. Debilitat animantium præsertim corpora, poros laxando, & internum calorem na-turæ

page.notes: The Greek heading reads roughly as "Ἔκθεσις"; the letters are faint and the accents are uncertain. The word "é-" at the start of the line "e-mollitio" has an uncertain accent. The catchword "turæ" is printed at the lower right, so it is not repeated in the text. The page has no marginal notes on the right side. The left strip shows the adjacent page and is excluded.
